FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.

2. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

3. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good morning / hello
   B. Excuse me
   C. Good night only
   D. Thank you

4. When practising Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.

5. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

6. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.

7. When practising Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.

8. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.

9. When practising Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

10. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. fenêtre
   B. chaise
   C. livre
   D. porte

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Guided reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for understanding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for understanding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

3. A — Good morning / hello

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information Vocabulary Grammar Attention.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking 1.2 Oral expression 1.3 Interactive listening 1.3 Active li.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.

9. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

10. C — livre

11. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for understanding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for understanding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
